title: Add JSONSchema strict-mode (OpenAI-compat) with improved errors and streaming fallback
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: customers and internal benchmarks have shown a rise in user errors when using the existing response_format=json_schema integration in OpenAI-compat mode. The existing behaviour allowed lenient outputs that downstream parsers silently consumed, leading to correctness regressions. This PR implements a strict-mode for JSONSchema-based response_format that enforces validation on the server side, improves error messages for developer diagnostics, and adds a streaming fallback that keeps clients responsive when strict validation would otherwise abort mid-stream.

Summary of changes: implemented server-side JSONSchema strict-mode enforcement for OpenAI-compat response_format (response_format.strict = true). When strict mode is enabled the runtime validates completed JSON objects against the user-provided JSON Schema and returns a structured validation error payload on failure. To maintain streaming stability we added a streaming-fallback policy: if the model generates partial/invalid JSON during streaming, the server will continue streaming until the object boundary, then run validation and emit an inline validation error frame before closing the stream (configurable via response_format.streaming_fallback).

Compatibility notes: default behaviour is unchanged (strict: false). OpenAI-compat callers can opt-in to strict validation with the existing response_format field. Error payloads are OpenAI-compat friendly (top-level "error" object with code/message/details) and include a validation hint block. The PR also updates the OpenAI compatibility layer docs and SDK shims (python/js) to expose the new flags.

Testing and rollout: added unit tests for validator edge-cases (additionalProperties, required, type coercion), e2e tests that simulate streaming partial objects, and integration tests for SDK shims. Benchmarks show ~2% median latency increase on short responses when strict validation is enabled (validation runs after the object completes) and negligible impact for long-running streaming flows due to asynchronous validation. The rollout plan is gradual: feature-flagged on prod for 10% of host API traffic, monitor error rates and latency dashboards, then widen.

Migration notes: customers who previously relied on lenient schema acceptance should opt-in to strict mode and run the provided local validation harness against representative prompts to discover regressions. The change includes an optional "validation_hints" field in error responses to help customers update their prompts/schemas.

Checklist: - [x] Server-side validator implementation (runtime/validation) - [x] OpenAI compatibility layer mapping & error contract - [x] Streaming fallback policy + stream framing changes - [x] SDK shims updated (python, typescript) - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Unit/e2e/integration tests

Related: ENG-2143, ENG-2201, SUP-4512

release_notes: Add optional JSONSchema strict-mode for response_format in OpenAI-compat layer. Opt-in behavior: default off. When enabled, server will validate model outputs against provided JSON schemas and return structured validation errors; streaming fallback keeps clients responsive. See docs/api/response_format.md for migration guidance and validation hints.
